domain_label: Study System — Nightly Analysis Mode & System Feedback Loops (sysloops)
purpose: A method for running the study system's nightly batch job as an idempotent, ordered pipeline — recompute retention actual-vs-predicted and its calibration, replay the day's answers through the skill models, cluster and diagnose weaknesses, build tomorrow's interleaved schedule within the time budget, gate the FSRS re-fit, and track the system's OWN metrics (prediction calibration, card-quality flags, schedule adherence, diagnosis efficacy, pipeline health) so the predictor+scheduler+content-factory improves itself instead of blaming the learner, keeping every design-synthesis claim tagged FACT / ESTIMATE / UNKNOWN against the cited learner-model machinery.
assumptions: no observed run of this system is supplied; sections 5-6 of the learner-model research are explicitly design synthesis [ESTIMATE], grounded in the cited FSRS / BKT / Elo / KST machinery but never observed here, so every scheduler threshold and cadence number is a labeled design default, not a measured operating point
the memory model (FSRS DSR) and its revlog, optimizer and leech mechanism are inherited as [FACT] from the repo file spaced_repetition_and_anki.md and are consumed, not re-derived, by this KB
the system is single-user, so population-scale models (DKT) are out and the per-skill models are BKT (per concept-tag) plus Elo (theta per concept, d per item) with a Glicko-style uncertainty proxy

the exact Glicko rating-deviation update equations are [UNKNOWN] in the grounding research (glicko.net was egress-blocked), so RD is used only as a conceptual uncertainty proxy and must not be hard-coded from memory until the canonical spec is fetched

the nightly job runs on the day's revlog rows, late-arriving AI-graded voice-answer transcriptions, the concept graph and yesterday's plan; all writes are append-only data snapshots, never in-place mutation of history
exclusions: the FSRS DSR formulas, revlog schema, optimizer internals and leech mechanism themselves (owned by the spaced-repetition specialist; consumed here as FACT)
the differential-diagnosis probe DESIGN and the E1-E4 error taxonomy internals (owned by the weakness-diagnosis specialist; this KB only invokes the procedure and schedules its probe items)
the concept graph / prerequisite ladder construction (owned by the flashcard-decomposition specialist; consumed here as an input the E3 back-off walks)
the flashcard-rewrite authoring and card-template design (owned by the flashcard-quality specialist; this KB only emits rewrite flags into that queue)
the gamification UI, calendar fill-bar rendering and voice-answer grading model itself (this KB only feeds them day-completion percentages and consumes the grading backlog age)
inventing exam pass rates, human RCT effect sizes, or any operating number the research file did not verify

competency_questions.question: What makes the nightly analysis a batch JOB rather than an online update, and why must every step be idempotent and ordered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the inputs (day's revlog, late graded voice answers, concept graph, yesterday's plan), the fixed step order, and that a crash mid-job must be safe to re-run producing the same result

competency_questions.question: How is retention calibration computed, and what makes the daily calibration snapshot a trend rather than a point?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: bins FSRS predicted-R (e.g. deciles) against observed recall, computes Brier / log-loss (log-loss = the FSRS optimizer's own objective, FACT), and stores a daily snapshot for trend lines

competency_questions.question: When may the FSRS memory parameters be re-fit, and why is refitting on thin data harmful?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: gates the re-fit behind ~1000+ total reviews AND ~2-4 weeks since the last fit, otherwise skips, because refitting on thin data adds noise; and reverts to prior parameters if calibration degrades after a fit

competency_questions.question: Which skill models update every night, and how is per-concept uncertainty represented given the Glicko gap?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: replays the day's answers through BKT (per concept-tag) and Elo (theta per concept, d per item), decays a Glicko-style uncertainty upward for untouched concepts, and flags the exact Glicko update equations as UNKNOWN / not to be hard-coded

competency_questions.question: How are weaknesses clustered and diagnosed nightly, and how do probe items avoid crowding out learning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: flags concepts with (low theta OR P(L) below threshold) AND low uncertainty, runs the differential-diagnosis procedure as far as data allows, and emits only a few probe items per day into tomorrow's queue

competency_questions.question: How does the confusion matrix detect discrimination failures, and why does it feed the interleaving policy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: maintains a concept x concept matrix of off-diagonal confusions (from tagged distractors or LLM-graded wrong-entity answers) and routes high-off-diagonal pairs into deliberately adjacent-but-not-identical interleaving

competency_questions.question: How does the nightly job flag bad CARDS instead of punishing the learner?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: detects leeches (repeated lapses), Elo item-difficulty outliers vs siblings, and extreme predicted-vs-actual gaps, and routes them to the flashcard-rewrite queue rather than lowering the learner's mastery

competency_questions.question: How is tomorrow's schedule assembled, ordered and trimmed to the time budget?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: composes due FSRS reviews + probe items + new-material quota, orders them by the interleaving rules, selects acquisition items at p ~= 0.85, and trims to budget by postponing mastered-easy items first, never weak-concept cards

competency_questions.question: What is the ~85% target, and why must the acquisition dial stay separate from the FSRS review-retention dial?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: cites the Eighty-Five-Percent Rule (Wilson et al. 2019, optimal error 15.87% for a class of learning algorithms, FACT with scope caveat), applies ~80-85% to NEW-material acquisition, and keeps it distinct from FSRS desired_retention (~0.9) which governs review

competency_questions.question: How is the challenge level re-calibrated from the rolling actuals?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: adjusts the target success band from the rolling 2-week success rate: loosen toward 0.7 when coasting (>92%), tighten toward 0.9 when frustrated (<70% or session abandonment)

competency_questions.question: What self-metrics does the system track about ITSELF, and what makes a metric worth keeping?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names the per-part scorecards (prediction calibration, skill-model sanity, card quality, schedule adherence, challenge calibration, diagnosis efficacy, pipeline health) and requires every metric to have a stored daily snapshot, a threshold, and a named action or flag or it is deleted

competency_questions.question: How does schedule adherence turn an unfinished plan into a fix for the PLAN, not a mark against the learner, and how does diagnosis efficacy improve the diagnosis loop itself?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: compares planned vs completed items/minutes and shrinks chronically ~60%-done plans (a plan never finished is a bad plan), and DIAGNOSIS_EFFICACY_LOOP checks whether theta/P(L) recovered within K days after a fix and adjusts the diagnosis thresholds when a fix class chronically fails

competency_questions.question: What is the reporting-artifact write contract, and why is nothing mutated in place?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: updates the learner KB (weakness records carrying the WHY), the gamification day-completion percentages and the self-metrics, all written as append-only data snapshots with no in-place mutation of history

competency_questions.question: When is a nightly run declared complete and valid, and what is the degraded-mode fallback?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: declares the run valid only when ingest reconciled, calibration snapshot stored, gated re-fit respected, weakness records emitted, schedule within budget and self-metrics updated, and specifies degraded mode = schedule on FSRS alone when the pipeline is unhealthy

glossary.definition: The system's owner-requested batch job that runs once per night over the day's data to recompute retention calibration, update the skill models, diagnose weaknesses, build tomorrow's schedule and refresh the system's self-metrics; a design-synthesis pipeline [ESTIMATE] grounded in the cited FSRS/BKT/Elo/KST machinery, not an observed run.

A pipeline step written so that re-running it (after a crash or a re-trigger) produces the same result and never double-counts; all writes are append-only data snapshots, never in-place mutation of the revlog or history.

The nightly comparison of FSRS predicted recall probability R against observed recall: bin reviews by predicted R (e.g. deciles), compare each bin's predicted vs actual recall rate, and score the fit with Brier / log-loss (log-loss is the exact objective the FSRS optimizer trains on, [FACT]).

The rule that the FSRS optimizer is re-run only when there are ~1000+ total reviews AND ~2-4 weeks since the last fit; otherwise the fit is skipped because refitting on thin data adds noise, and prior parameters are reverted to if calibration degrades after a fit.

The per-concept mastery layer distinct from the per-card memory model: BKT gives an interpretable P(knows concept-tag) from four HMM parameters, Elo rates learner theta per concept and difficulty d per item in O(1) online updates (a streaming Rasch/1PL approximation, [FACT]); a Glicko-style uncertainty is decayed upward for untouched concepts.

A rating-deviation-like measure of how sure the system is that a weakness is real versus under-sampled; used conceptually to decide when to probe, but the exact Glicko update equations are [UNKNOWN] here (glicko.net was egress-blocked in the grounding research) and must not be hard-coded from memory until fetched.

A concept x concept matrix M where M[i][j] counts 'asked about i, answered with j's content' (from misconception-tagged distractors or LLM-graded wrong-entity free/spoken answers); high off-diagonal pairs mark discrimination failures and become the exact pairs to interleave.

A diagnostic question emitted by the nightly weakness pass to test which of the E1-E4 causes explains a flagged weakness; only a few are injected per day so diagnosis never crowds out learning in tomorrow's queue.

The Eighty-Five-Percent Rule (Wilson, Shenhav, Straccia & Cohen, Nature Communications 10:4646, 2019): for a class of gradient-descent learning algorithms on binary tasks the learning rate is maximized at ~85% training accuracy (optimal error 15.87%, [FACT]); applied as a principled default target for NEW-material acquisition (~80-85%), kept separate from the FSRS review-retention dial (~0.9).

The set of scorecards the system keeps about ITSELF (prediction calibration, skill-model sanity, card quality, schedule adherence, challenge calibration, diagnosis efficacy, pipeline health); the governing principle is that every metric must have a stored daily snapshot, a threshold, and a named automatic action or human-visible flag, or it is deleted.

Planned vs completed items/minutes, time-of-day completion pattern and mid-session abandonment; a plan that is chronically only ~60% done is treated as a bad plan (to be shrunk), not a bad learner, and it feeds the calendar fill-bar UI honestly.

The fallback the go/no-go names when the pipeline is unhealthy (nightly-job failure, stale voice-grading backlog, high ungraded count): schedule on FSRS due reviews alone, skipping the skill-model and diagnosis steps, rather than shipping a bad or empty plan.

nodes.definition: Establish the nightly analysis as a BATCH JOB with a contract, the fact that shapes every downstream step [ESTIMATE: design synthesis, grounded in the cited machinery]. Inputs: the day's revlog rows (one row per review ever, [FACT - repo FSRS file]), any late-arriving AI-graded voice-answer transcriptions, the concept graph and yesterday's plan. The pipeline is ordered (ingest -> calibration -> skill update -> weakness/card passes -> schedule -> self-metrics -> report) and every step is idempotent: a crash mid-job must be safe to re-run and produce the same result. Cadence: most steps run nightly, the FSRS re-fit runs weekly-to-monthly (its own gate). Writes are append-only snapshots, never in-place mutation of history.

included: the four inputs and the fixed step order
idempotency / crash-safe re-run
the nightly-vs-weekly cadence split and append-only write rule
excluded: the internal formulas of any single step
the FSRS model internals it consumes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new input stream, an idempotency violation, or a cadence change updates the job contract

pros.claim: Framing the analysis as an ordered idempotent job makes a mid-run crash recoverable and stops double-counted or half-applied updates
pros.example: a power loss after the skill update but before scheduling simply re-runs the whole job to the same state

cons.claim: A fixed order and idempotency discipline add engineering overhead versus ad hoc online updates
cons.example: having to make every write append-only rather than mutating a running tally in place

failure_modes: mutating the revlog or plan in place so a re-run double-counts
letting steps run out of order so calibration reads stale skill state
acceptance_tests: the contract names the four inputs, the fixed ordered steps, the nightly-vs-weekly cadence, and the crash-safe idempotent re-run guarantee with append-only writes
revisit_triggers: a new input stream (e.g. a new answer format) is added to the job
a re-run is found to double-count, showing a step is not idempotent
the cadence split changes

nodes.definition: Run step 1: ingest and reconcile the day's data before any analysis touches it. Pull the day's review rows and any late-arriving AI-graded voice-answer transcriptions, attach concept-tags to each, and reconcile duplicates / out-of-order arrivals so the downstream math sees one clean event stream [ESTIMATE: design synthesis]. Late voice grades that arrive after their review must be joined back to the original attempt, not counted as new attempts. This is the idempotency anchor of the whole job: it is written so re-running it over the same day yields the identical tagged event set, which is what lets every later step be safely re-run.

included: pulling the day's reviews + late graded voice answers
concept-tagging and duplicate/order reconciliation
the join of late grades back to their original attempt
excluded: the voice-answer grading model itself
the calibration and skill math that consume the clean stream

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new grading source or a reconciliation error changes the ingest step

pros.claim: Reconciling late voice grades onto their original attempt keeps recall statistics honest and idempotent
pros.example: a spoken answer graded the next morning updating yesterday's attempt rather than inflating today's review count

cons.claim: Waiting to reconcile late-arriving grades can delay a concept's flag by a day
cons.example: a weakness only becoming visible once the backlogged voice grade lands

failure_modes: counting a late-graded voice answer as a fresh attempt and double-counting recall
leaving reviews untagged so concept-level aggregation misses them
acceptance_tests: the step reconciles the day's reviews and late graded voice answers into one concept-tagged, de-duplicated event stream that is identical on re-run
revisit_triggers: a new answer/grading source is added
duplicate or mis-joined late grades surface
concept-tag coverage gaps appear

nodes.definition: Run step 2: score how well the memory model predicted the day's recall. For every review, take the FSRS predicted recall R at that moment, bin reviews by predicted R (e.g. deciles), and compare each bin's predicted vs observed recall rate to produce a per-bin calibration table; summarize the fit with Brier score and log-loss (log-loss is the exact objective the FSRS optimizer trains on, [FACT - repo FSRS file]). Store the result as a daily calibration SNAPSHOT so the system tracks a trend line, not a single point. A well-calibrated model has each decile's observed recall near its predicted value; systematic gaps are the signal the prediction-calibration self-loop and the re-fit gate act on.

included: binning predicted R vs observed recall and the per-bin table
Brier / log-loss scoring and the daily snapshot for trend
excluded: the decision to re-fit (the gate node)
the FSRS formula that produced R

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a persistent calibration drift or a re-fit re-baseline changes the snapshot reading

pros.claim: A binned predicted-vs-actual table plus a stored trend makes model drift visible before it silently degrades scheduling
pros.example: the 0.9-1.0 predicted-R decile recalling at only 0.78 flags an over-optimistic model

cons.claim: On a single user's daily volume the bins are thin, so a one-day snapshot is noisy and only the trend is trustworthy
cons.example: a decile with three reviews swinging the daily Brier score by chance

failure_modes: reading a single noisy daily snapshot as a real degradation and refitting prematurely
computing recall on un-reconciled events so calibration is wrong
acceptance_tests: the step bins FSRS predicted R against observed recall, computes Brier and log-loss, and stores a dated daily calibration snapshot for the trend line
revisit_triggers: the calibration trend drifts persistently
a re-fit lands and the post-fit calibration must be re-baselined
the binning scheme (decile count) is changed

nodes.definition: Run step 3: decide whether to re-fit the FSRS memory parameters, and usually decide NOT to. Re-run the FSRS optimizer on the revlog (py-fsrs / fsrs-rs expose an optimize entry point, [FACT - repo FSRS file]) ONLY when there are ~1000+ total reviews AND ~2-4 weeks since the last fit; otherwise skip, because refitting on thin data adds noise rather than signal [ESTIMATE: design synthesis, thresholds are labeled defaults]. This is the one weekly-to-monthly step in an otherwise nightly job. After a fit, the prediction-calibration loop checks whether calibration improved; if it degraded, revert to the previous parameters. The gate protects the scheduler from chasing noise between fits.

included: the ~1000-review and ~2-4-week gate
running vs skipping the FSRS optimize
the revert-on-degradation rule
excluded: the FSRS optimizer internals
the calibration computation itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a threshold miss or a post-fit degradation changes the re-fit gate

pros.claim: Gating the re-fit behind data-volume and recency thresholds stops noisy parameter churn that would destabilize scheduling
pros.example: skipping a re-fit at 300 reviews so the model is not overfit to two weeks of thin data

cons.claim: A conservative gate can leave the model stale for weeks after the learner's memory behaviour genuinely shifts
cons.example: a real change in retention going untracked because the 2-4-week window has not elapsed

failure_modes: refitting on thin data and injecting noise into every interval
keeping degraded parameters after a bad fit because no post-fit calibration check runs
acceptance_tests: the gate runs the FSRS optimize only at ~1000+ reviews and ~2-4 weeks since last fit, otherwise skips, and reverts parameters if post-fit calibration degrades
revisit_triggers: the review-volume or recency threshold proves too tight or too loose
a post-fit calibration degradation forces a revert
a new optimizer version changes the re-fit cost

nodes.definition: Run step 4: replay the day's reconciled answers through the per-concept skill models (distinct from the per-card FSRS memory model). BKT updates an interpretable P(knows concept-tag) via its four-parameter HMM update on each correct/incorrect observation [FACT - BKT update equations, Corbett & Anderson 1995 lineage]; Elo updates learner theta per concept and difficulty d per item with O(1) online steps (theta <- theta + K(y - p), p = 1/(1+e^-(theta-d)); Elo is a streaming Rasch/1PL approximation, [FACT]). MCQ corrects are down-weighted for the ~25% guessing floor of a 4-option item [FACT - IRT 3PL c-parameter]. A Glicko-style uncertainty is decayed UPWARD for concepts untouched more than N days; the exact Glicko rating-deviation equations are [UNKNOWN] here (glicko.net was egress-blocked) and are used only as a conceptual proxy, never hard-coded from memory.

included: the BKT and Elo nightly replay and their update forms
the MCQ guessing-floor down-weighting
the Glicko-style uncertainty decay with the UNKNOWN-equations caveat
excluded: population-scale DKT (out for a single user)
the differential-diagnosis procedure that consumes the flags

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fetching the Glicko spec or detecting a skill-model divergence changes the replay

pros.claim: Running BKT and Elo together gives both an interpretable mastery number and a matched learner-vs-item difficulty, from the first handful of answers
pros.example: reporting P(knows periodontal-anatomy)=0.72 while Elo places the concept's items at a matched difficulty

cons.claim: The Glicko-style uncertainty is only a proxy until the canonical equations are fetched, so 'how sure is this weakness' is approximate
cons.example: an untouched concept's uncertainty decayed by a hand-chosen rule rather than the real RD update

failure_modes: hard-coding Glicko update equations from memory instead of treating RD as an UNKNOWN-blocked proxy
treating an MCQ correct as full mastery evidence and ignoring the guessing floor
acceptance_tests: the step replays the day's answers through BKT and Elo, down-weights MCQ corrects for the guessing floor, decays a Glicko-style uncertainty upward for untouched concepts, and marks the exact Glicko equations UNKNOWN / not-hard-coded
revisit_triggers: the canonical Glicko update equations are fetched and the RD proxy can be replaced
a skill-model divergence or degeneracy is detected
a new answer format changes the guessing-floor weighting

nodes.definition: Guard the skill models against degenerate fits (the skill-model-sanity self-scorecard). BKT can 'explain' performance as pure guessing or slipping instead of knowledge, so constrain P(G) < ~0.3 and P(S) < ~0.1-0.3 and reject fits that breach the caps [ESTIMATE: high confidence - standard BKT practice]. For Elo, watch for theta/d divergence (a runaway rating). When a nightly fit is degenerate, freeze it and fall back to the previous parameters rather than shipping a broken mastery estimate into scheduling. This is a guardrail node: it never improves the model, it only prevents a bad fit from reaching tomorrow's plan.

included: the P(G) and P(S) degeneracy caps
Elo theta/d divergence detection
freeze-and-fall-back-to-previous on a bad fit
excluded: the nightly BKT/Elo update math itself
the weakness diagnosis that consumes clean flags

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a slipped degenerate fit or a mis-tuned cap changes the guard

pros.claim: Capping guess/slip and reverting degenerate fits stops a mathematically-fine but meaningless mastery estimate from driving the schedule
pros.example: rejecting a BKT fit that set P(G)=0.5 to 'explain' a hard concept as guessing

cons.claim: Hard caps can suppress a genuinely high guess rate on a truly guessable item format
cons.example: a true four-option-MCQ concept legitimately near the guessing floor being flagged degenerate

failure_modes: shipping a degenerate fit because no cap check runs
capping so aggressively that real guess-heavy formats are misread
acceptance_tests: the guard checks P(G) and P(S) against their caps and Elo for divergence, and on a breach freezes the fit and falls back to previous parameters
revisit_triggers: a degenerate fit slips through and reaches the schedule
the caps prove mis-tuned for a format
a new skill model is added needing its own sanity check

nodes.definition: Recompute the concept x concept confusion matrix M where M[i][j] counts 'asked about i, answered with j's content', drawn from misconception-tagged distractors and LLM-graded free/spoken answers that name the wrong entity [ESTIMATE: design synthesis; the misconception-distractor signal it consumes is FACT - Eedi-style distractor tagging]. High off-diagonal pairs (two drugs, two nerves, two TOEFL word-senses) are discrimination failures, a subtype of misconception (E2). The matrix is the data source the interleaving policy reads: the exact pairs the learner confuses are the pairs to interleave adjacent-but-not-identical, because interleaving is what trains discrimination.

included: building M from tagged distractors and wrong-entity graded answers
flagging high off-diagonal pairs as discrimination failures
handing confused pairs to the interleaving policy
excluded: the interleaving queue ordering itself
the full E1-E4 taxonomy internals

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a recurring confused pair or a grading-source change updates the matrix

pros.claim: A concept-confusion matrix turns vague 'gets these mixed up' into a ranked list of exact pairs to interleave
pros.example: surfacing that two adjacent nerves are repeatedly swapped and scheduling them as a contrast pair

cons.claim: Off-diagonal counts are sparse for a single user, so a pair can look confused on one coincidence
cons.example: a single mislabeled distractor answer inflating a pair that is not truly confused

failure_modes: interleaving pairs flagged from one-off noise
missing a confusion because free-answer wrong-entity naming was not graded into the matrix
acceptance_tests: the matrix counts wrong-entity answers per concept pair, flags high off-diagonal pairs as discrimination failures, and passes them to the interleaving policy
revisit_triggers: a confused pair recurs enough to warrant a dedicated contrast card
the distractor-tagging or grading source changes
a flagged pair turns out to be noise

nodes.definition: Run step 5: cluster and diagnose weaknesses, producing the 'why' the owner asked for. Flag concepts with (low Elo theta OR BKT P(L) below threshold) AND low uncertainty (a well-measured weakness, not an under-sampled one). For each flag, run the differential-diagnosis decision procedure as far as existing data allows: rule out a slip (E1), test retrieval decay (E4) vs never-learned using FSRS predicted-R at failure time, walk down the prerequisite graph (E3), and probe misconception distractors (E2). Whatever stays ambiguous emits a few PROBE ITEMS into tomorrow's queue [ESTIMATE: probe-design synthesis; the mechanisms - BKT slip, FSRS R, KST fringe, distractor tagging - are FACT]. Output is a weakness record {concept, cause in E1-E4, evidence, prescribed fix} written to the learner KB.

included: flagging (low theta OR low P(L)) AND low-uncertainty concepts
running the E1-E4 differential diagnosis as far as data allows
emitting a few probe items and the weakness record
excluded: authoring the probe/contrast content (diagnosis specialist)
the scheduling of probes into the queue (schedule node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a chronic fix failure or a probe-budget overrun changes the diagnosis step

pros.claim: Requiring low uncertainty before flagging stops the system chasing under-sampled concepts, and the E1-E4 procedure gives an actionable cause not just a location
pros.example: diagnosing a failure as a missing prerequisite (E3) and remediating the deepest failing prereq first

cons.claim: Diagnosis is data-hungry, so many flags stay ambiguous and can only be resolved by probes over several days
cons.example: an E2-vs-E3 ambiguity unresolved until distractor probes accumulate

failure_modes: flagging under-sampled concepts as real weaknesses
letting probe items grow until diagnosis crowds out learning in the queue
acceptance_tests: the step flags well-measured weak concepts, runs the E1-E4 differential diagnosis to the limit of data, emits a small daily probe budget, and writes a weakness record with cause and prescribed fix
revisit_triggers: a diagnosed fix class chronically fails (the efficacy loop feeds back thresholds)
the probe budget starts crowding learning
a new error-cause category is added

nodes.definition: Run step 6: score the CARDS, not the learner. Detect leeches (cards with repeated lapses via Anki's native leech mechanism, [FACT - repo FSRS file]), Elo item-difficulty outliers whose d has drifted far above their concept siblings, and cards whose predicted-vs-actual recall gap is extreme. Route these to the flashcard-rewrite queue for the card-quality specialist rather than lowering the learner's mastery estimate [ESTIMATE: design synthesis]. The governing idea: a card the whole population of the learner's attempts fails is more likely a bad card than a real weakness, so a bad card must not be recorded as a learner weakness.

included: leech, item-Elo-outlier and predicted-vs-actual-gap detection
routing to the rewrite queue instead of penalizing the learner
excluded: authoring the rewrite (card-quality specialist)
the per-template aggregation (its own loop)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a template-level underperformance or a mis-flagged hard card changes the card pass

pros.claim: Separating bad cards from real weaknesses prevents a defective card from being logged forever as a learner deficit
pros.example: an ambiguous card that everyone lapses on going to rewrite rather than dragging down its concept's mastery

cons.claim: A genuine hard-but-correct card can look like a bad card and be needlessly flagged for rewrite
cons.example: a legitimately difficult discrimination card flagged as an Elo outlier

failure_modes: recording a bad card's failures as a learner weakness
flagging a legitimately hard card for rewrite and losing desirable difficulty
acceptance_tests: the pass detects leeches, item-Elo outliers and extreme predicted-vs-actual gaps and routes them to the rewrite queue without lowering the learner's mastery
revisit_triggers: a whole card TEMPLATE type underperforms (the card-quality loop escalates)
a rewrite-flagged card turns out to have been correctly hard
the leech threshold is re-tuned

nodes.definition: Establish the ~85% success target as a design constant the scheduler aims at for NEW-material acquisition. The Eighty-Five-Percent Rule (Wilson, Shenhav, Straccia & Cohen, Nature Communications 10:4646, 2019) shows that for a broad class of gradient-descent learning algorithms on binary tasks the learning rate is maximized at ~85% training accuracy, optimal error 15.87% [FACT, with the scope caveat that this is a result about learning ALGORITHMS, not a direct human RCT]. Apply it as a principled default acquisition target (~80-85% correct), and keep it strictly separate from the FSRS review-retention dial (desired_retention ~0.9, owner-tunable 0.8-0.97, [FACT]) which governs a different quantity (retention of learned cards, not accuracy on new practice). Conflating the two mis-tunes both.

included: the 85% rule and its 15.87% optimal error with the algorithm-not-human scope caveat
applying ~80-85% to acquisition
keeping it separate from the FSRS ~0.9 review-retention dial
excluded: the runtime challenge re-calibration from actuals (its own node)
the FSRS retention machinery itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a human-subject result or a rolling-actuals mismatch revises the acquisition target

pros.claim: A single principled acquisition target lets the scheduler pick items at a known difficulty instead of guessing
pros.example: selecting new-material items whose p(theta,d) is ~0.85 so practice is hard-but-winnable

cons.claim: The 85% figure is an algorithmic result, not a human law, so it is a default to tune, not a guarantee
cons.example: treating 85% as sacred for a learner whose optimal challenge band differs

failure_modes: conflating the acquisition target with the FSRS review-retention dial and mis-tuning both
presenting the 85% figure as a proven human law rather than a scoped default
acceptance_tests: the node cites the 85% rule and 15.87% optimal error with the algorithm-not-human caveat and keeps the acquisition target distinct from the FSRS review-retention dial
revisit_triggers: the rolling actuals show the learner's best band is not ~85%
a human-subject result refines the target
the FSRS desired_retention dial is retuned and the separation must be re-checked

nodes.definition: Run step 8: re-calibrate the challenge band from the rolling actuals. Using the acquisition target as the anchor, adjust the live target success band from the rolling 2-week success rate: loosen toward 0.7 when the learner is coasting (rolling success > ~92%) and tighten toward 0.9 when frustrated (success < ~70% or session abandonment) [ESTIMATE: design synthesis; anchored on the FACT 85% rule]. With Elo in place this is one line: select next items whose difficulty d makes p(theta,d) land in the current band. The band is a control signal for tomorrow's acquisition-item selection, driven by desirable-difficulty logic (fluency in-session is a misleading signal; judge by delayed retrieval, [FACT - Bjork]).

included: adjusting the target band from the rolling 2-week success rate
the coasting-loosen and frustrated-tighten rules
the desirable-difficulty framing of the band
excluded: the 85% target derivation (its own node)
the queue ordering that consumes the band

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a whipsawing band or a threshold change updates the challenge calibration

pros.claim: A rolling band adapts challenge to the learner's actual state instead of a static difficulty
pros.example: loosening toward 0.7 for a coasting week to push growth, tightening toward 0.9 when abandonment spikes

cons.claim: A short rolling window can overreact to a bad week or a distracted stretch
cons.example: tightening the band after a single frustrating session that was really about fatigue

failure_modes: overreacting to a noisy short window and whipsawing the difficulty
optimizing for in-session fluency instead of delayed retrieval
acceptance_tests: the step adjusts the target band from the rolling 2-week success rate with the coasting-loosen and frustrated-tighten rules and selects acquisition items to land in-band
revisit_triggers: the band whipsaws, indicating the window is too short
abandonment patterns change the frustrated threshold
the anchor acquisition target is revised

nodes.definition: Define the queue-ordering policy the schedule builder applies: never drill one concept-tag in a long block once past first exposure; the daily queue mixes tags, with confused-pair items (from the confusion matrix) placed deliberately adjacent-but-not-identical; blocking is allowed only for the very first encounter with a topic (initial encoding) [ESTIMATE: synthesis; grounded in FACT interleaving evidence - Rohrer et al. 2020 delayed-test 61% vs 38%, d=0.83, and Brunmair & Richter 2019 g=0.42, effects smaller/mixed for math]. Interleaving works chiefly where items are confusable, which is why the confusion matrix feeds this policy directly. This node supplies the ORDER; the schedule builder supplies the content set.

included: the mix-tags / no-long-blocks rule
adjacent-but-not-identical placement of confused pairs
blocking only at first encounter
excluded: the content selection and budget trim (schedule node)
the confusion-matrix construction (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a material-type exception or a confused-pair source change updates the ordering

pros.claim: Interleaving confusable pairs trains the discrimination that blocked practice hides behind in-session fluency
pros.example: spacing two confused word-senses across the queue so the learner must discriminate, not pattern-match

cons.claim: Interleaving's benefit is smaller and mixed for some material (e.g. math), so a blanket rule can hurt initial encoding
cons.example: interleaving a brand-new topic before it is encoded once, per the mixed math results

failure_modes: interleaving a topic's very first encounter and breaking initial encoding
placing confused pairs identically adjacent so the learner copies rather than discriminates
acceptance_tests: the policy mixes tags after first exposure, places confused pairs adjacent-but-not-identical, and blocks only initial encounters
revisit_triggers: a material type shows interleaving hurting (mixed-evidence case)
the confused-pair source changes
first-encounter handling needs adjustment

nodes.definition: Compute tomorrow's predicted review load from the stability (S) distribution and trim it to the owner's time budget by the correct priority order: postpone MASTERED-EASY cards first (lowest predicted-R loss) and never postpone weak-concept cards [ESTIMATE: design synthesis; the S-distribution load computation and the D/S easiness signal are FACT - repo FSRS file]. Easiness is read off FSRS: concepts with low mean difficulty D, high median stability S and Elo theta well above item d are 'mastered-easy' and can take longer initial steps while the specialist stops generating fresh drills there. The trim is what keeps the plan inside the time budget without dropping the items that matter.

included: predicting daily load from the S distribution
trimming to budget by postponing mastered-easy first
the D+S+theta mastered-easy signal
excluded: the interleaving order (its own node)
the final assembled queue (schedule node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a postponed-easy lapse or a time-budget change updates the trim

pros.claim: Trimming by postponing mastered-easy first keeps the plan inside the time budget at the lowest cost to retention
pros.example: deferring a batch of high-stability easy reviews rather than skipping a weak-concept drill

cons.claim: Repeatedly postponing mastered-easy cards can let their intervals overstretch if the trim runs many days in a row
cons.example: an easy card drifting past its optimal review because it was postponed every night in a busy week

failure_modes: trimming weak-concept cards to fit the budget instead of mastered-easy ones
over-postponing easy cards until their retention actually lapses
acceptance_tests: the step predicts load from the S distribution and trims to the time budget by postponing mastered-easy (lowest predicted-R loss) cards first, never weak-concept cards
revisit_triggers: a postponed-easy card lapses, showing the trim overreached
the owner's time budget changes
the mastered-easy signal is re-tuned

nodes.definition: Run step 7: assemble tomorrow's schedule from the parts. Content set = due FSRS reviews + the day's probe items + the new-material quota; order it by the interleaving policy; select acquisition items at p ~= 0.85 (via the challenge band); trim to the time budget by postponing mastered-easy first [ESTIMATE: design synthesis; each input is FACT/estimate per its own node]. Probe items are capped so diagnosis never crowds out learning. If the pipeline is unhealthy, fall back to degraded mode (FSRS due reviews alone). The output is a concrete, budget-bounded, interleaved queue for the next day and the plan-of-record that schedule adherence is later measured against.

included: combining due reviews + probes + new-material quota
applying interleaving order, the ~0.85 acquisition band and the budget trim
the degraded-mode fall-back to FSRS-only
excluded: the internal computation of each input (their own nodes)
the reporting write (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: chronic non-completion or a quota/cap retune changes the schedule build

pros.claim: One assembly step composes memory, diagnosis, difficulty and budget into a single concrete plan-of-record
pros.example: a queue that mixes due reviews, two probes and new items at ~0.85 difficulty, trimmed to 30 minutes

cons.claim: The plan is only as good as its inputs, so a bad flag or mis-calibrated band propagates straight into the queue
cons.example: an over-tight challenge band making the whole next day feel frustrating

failure_modes: letting probe items exceed their cap and crowd out learning
shipping a full plan when the pipeline is unhealthy instead of degrading to FSRS-only
acceptance_tests: the builder composes due reviews + capped probes + new-material quota, orders by interleaving, selects acquisition at p~=0.85, trims by postponing mastered-easy, and degrades to FSRS-only when unhealthy
revisit_triggers: schedule adherence shows the plan is chronically unfinished
a probe cap or new-material quota is retuned
degraded mode is triggered and its plan must be reviewed

nodes.definition: The prediction-calibration self-loop: track the per-decile predicted-R-vs-actual table and the Brier / log-loss TREND across days, not just tonight's snapshot. Its threshold-and-action contract: a persistent degradation triggers the FSRS re-fit gate, and — critically — if calibration gets WORSE after a fit, revert to the previous parameters [ESTIMATE: design synthesis; log-loss objective and the optimizer are FACT]. This is the scorecard for the predictor half of the system; it consumes the daily calibration snapshots and turns their trend into a re-fit-or-revert decision.

included: the Brier/log-loss trend across daily snapshots
triggering the re-fit on persistent degradation
revert-after-a-worse-fit
excluded: the nightly calibration computation (its own node)
the re-fit gate thresholds (their own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a noise-triggered fire or a threshold retune changes the calibration loop

pros.claim: Watching the calibration trend and reverting bad fits keeps the predictor from silently degrading the schedule
pros.example: rolling back a re-fit whose next-week Brier score rose above the pre-fit baseline

cons.claim: Trend detection needs enough days to separate drift from noise, so it reacts slowly by design
cons.example: waiting a week of snapshots before confirming a real degradation

failure_modes: reacting to a single noisy snapshot instead of the trend
keeping a worse post-fit parameter set because no revert check runs
acceptance_tests: the loop tracks the Brier/log-loss trend, triggers a re-fit on persistent degradation, and reverts parameters when calibration worsens after a fit
revisit_triggers: the trend detector fires on noise
a revert is triggered and must be reviewed
the degradation threshold is retuned

nodes.definition: The schedule-adherence self-loop: compare tomorrow's plan (once it becomes today) against what was actually completed — planned vs completed items/minutes, time-of-day completion pattern, and mid-session abandonment [ESTIMATE: design synthesis]. Its governing rule: a plan that is chronically only ~60% done is a BAD PLAN to be shrunk, not a bad learner to be blamed; the loop feeds the schedule builder to size future plans realistically and feeds the calendar fill-bar UI honestly. This is the scorecard for the scheduler half of the system, measured from plan vs revlog.

included: planned-vs-completed items/minutes, time-of-day and abandonment tracking
shrinking chronically-under-completed plans
honest fill-bar feed
excluded: the schedule assembly itself (its own node)
the gamification UI rendering

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a post-shrink recheck or a threshold retune changes the adherence loop

pros.claim: Treating an unfinished plan as a planning fault keeps the system honest and the learner un-blamed
pros.example: shrinking a plan that is completed only 60% for a week so it becomes finishable

cons.claim: Shrinking plans on adherence alone can under-challenge a learner who is capable but was briefly busy
cons.example: cutting the plan after one hectic week the learner would otherwise have caught up on

failure_modes: blaming the learner for a chronically unfinishable plan
shrinking a plan on a one-off busy stretch and under-challenging
acceptance_tests: the loop measures planned vs completed items/minutes and abandonment and shrinks chronically ~60%-done plans while feeding the fill-bar honestly
revisit_triggers: a plan is shrunk and its next-week completion must be re-checked
abandonment patterns shift
the ~60% chronic threshold is retuned

nodes.definition: The diagnosis-efficacy self-loop, the one that improves the loop: after a weakness was diagnosed E2/E3/E4 and its prescribed fix applied, check whether theta / P(L) actually recovered within K days [ESTIMATE: design synthesis]. If a fix CLASS chronically fails to produce recovery, the DIAGNOSIS PROCEDURE itself — the E1-E4 thresholds and probe logic in the weakness step — gets adjusted, rather than repeating an ineffective remediation. This closes the meta-loop: the system audits not just the learner's weaknesses but its own ability to diagnose and fix them.

included: the K-day recovery check per applied fix
adjusting the diagnosis thresholds when a fix class chronically fails
excluded: the diagnosis procedure internals (weakness node)
authoring the remediation content

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a chronic fix failure or a K-window change updates the efficacy loop

pros.claim: Auditing whether fixes actually work lets the diagnosis procedure self-correct instead of repeating dead remediations
pros.example: loosening an E3 back-off threshold after prerequisite remediation repeatedly fails to lift the surface concept

cons.claim: Recovery within K days is a coarse signal that can miss slow or confounded improvement
cons.example: a fix that works over a month being judged a failure at K=7 days

failure_modes: repeating a fix class that never produces recovery
adjusting the procedure on too-short a recovery window and destabilizing diagnosis
acceptance_tests: the loop checks theta/P(L) recovery within K days after a fix and adjusts the diagnosis thresholds when a fix class chronically fails
revisit_triggers: a fix class is found chronically ineffective
the K-day window proves too short
a new fix class is added and needs an efficacy baseline

nodes.definition: The card-quality self-loop: aggregate the nightly card-quality flags into rates the system watches over time — leech rate, item-Elo outlier count, per-card lapse rate and per-TEMPLATE error rate [ESTIMATE: design synthesis; leech mechanism is FACT]. Its distinct escalation: when a whole card TYPE (template) underperforms, fix it at the template level rather than one card at a time, and feed the rewrite queue for the flashcard specialist. This is the scorecard for the content-factory half of the system; it turns single-card flags into template-level and trend-level content fixes.

included: aggregating leech rate, item-Elo outliers, lapse rate and per-template error rate
template-level escalation and the rewrite-queue feed
excluded: the nightly single-card detection (its own node)
authoring the rewrite (card-quality specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a template threshold crossing or a post-fix re-measure changes the card-quality loop

pros.claim: Aggregating to the template level catches a systematic content flaw one-card-at-a-time flags would miss
pros.example: spotting that a whole cloze-template family errors high and fixing the template once

cons.claim: Template-level rates need volume to be trustworthy, so early on they are thin
cons.example: a template flagged on only a few cards' worth of evidence

failure_modes: fixing cards one at a time when a whole template is the fault
acting on a thin template rate before it is meaningful
acceptance_tests: the loop aggregates leech rate, item-Elo outliers, lapse rate and per-template error rate and escalates underperforming templates to a template-level fix and the rewrite queue
revisit_triggers: a template rate crosses its threshold
a template fix lands and its effect must be re-measured
a new card template is introduced

nodes.definition: The pipeline-health self-loop: track nightly-job completion, voice-answer grading backlog age and ungraded-item count from the job logs [ESTIMATE: design synthesis]. Its action contract: alert on failures, and when the pipeline is unhealthy enter DEGRADED MODE — schedule on FSRS due reviews alone, skipping the skill-model and diagnosis steps — rather than shipping an empty or corrupt plan. This is the scorecard for the plumbing; it is the safety net that guarantees the learner always gets at least a valid FSRS review plan even when the analysis stack is down.

included: job-completion, grading-backlog-age and ungraded-count tracking
alerting and the degraded-mode FSRS-only fallback
excluded: the voice-grading model itself
the full go/no-go composition (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a long degraded episode or an alert-threshold retune changes the health loop

pros.claim: A health scorecard with a degraded-mode fallback guarantees a valid plan even when the analysis stack fails
pros.example: a failed skill-update step still yielding an FSRS-only review plan instead of no plan

cons.claim: Degraded mode drops the diagnosis and challenge benefits, so a long outage quietly reduces the system to plain SRS
cons.example: days of FSRS-only plans with no weakness probes while a grading backlog clears

failure_modes: shipping a corrupt or empty plan instead of degrading to FSRS-only
letting a grading backlog age silently without an alert
acceptance_tests: the loop tracks job completion, grading-backlog age and ungraded count, alerts on failure, and enters FSRS-only degraded mode when the pipeline is unhealthy
revisit_triggers: a degraded-mode episode runs long enough to matter
the backlog-age alert threshold is retuned
a new pipeline stage needs a health signal

nodes.definition: Compose the system's self-metrics into one governed scorecard set (prediction calibration, skill-model sanity, card quality, schedule adherence, challenge calibration, diagnosis efficacy, pipeline health) and enforce the governing principle: every metric MUST have (a) a stored daily snapshot (a trend, not a point), (b) a threshold, and (c) a named automatic action or human-visible flag — a metric with no consumer is deleted [ESTIMATE: design synthesis]. This is the meta-node of section 6: it is what makes the system a self-auditing predictor+scheduler+content-factory rather than a black box, and it is the source of the reporting artifacts' self-metrics block.

included: the roster of self-scorecards
the snapshot+threshold+named-consumer rule
deleting any metric with no consumer
excluded: each loop's internal computation (their own nodes)
the reporting write mechanics (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new loop, an orphan metric, or a threshold-action revision updates the scorecard

pros.claim: Requiring every metric to have a snapshot, threshold and named consumer stops vanity metrics and keeps the scorecard actionable
pros.example: deleting a tracked number that no action or flag ever reads

cons.claim: Strict governance can prune an early-signal metric before its consumer is built
cons.example: removing a promising metric because its automated action is not yet wired

failure_modes: accumulating metrics no action consumes
pruning a metric whose consumer was merely not-yet-built
acceptance_tests: the scorecard lists the self-loops and enforces that each metric has a daily snapshot, a threshold and a named action or flag, deleting any without a consumer
revisit_triggers: a new self-loop is added to the roster
a metric is found with no consumer
a threshold-to-action mapping is revised

nodes.definition: Run step 9: write the night's outputs as append-only data artifacts. Update the learner KB with the weakness records (each carrying the WHY — cause E1-E4, evidence, prescribed fix), refresh the gamification layer's day-completion percentages, and persist the self-metrics snapshots [ESTIMATE: design synthesis]. Everything is written as new dated data; there is NO in-place mutation of history, which is what preserves idempotency and lets any step be re-run. These artifacts are the job's contract with the rest of the system: the learner UI, the gamification calendar and the self-audit trail all read from here.

included: writing weakness records with the WHY, day-completion percentages and self-metrics snapshots
the append-only no-in-place-mutation write rule
excluded: the UI/gamification rendering
the computation of the artifacts' contents

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a retention policy, a new consumer field, or an idempotency break updates the reporting step

pros.claim: Append-only artifact writes preserve idempotency and give every consumer a stable, auditable record
pros.example: re-running the job re-emits the same dated snapshot instead of corrupting yesterday's record

cons.claim: Append-only storage grows without bound and needs a retention/rollup policy over time
cons.example: years of daily self-metric snapshots needing compaction

failure_modes: mutating a prior record in place and breaking re-run idempotency
writing a weakness record without its cause/evidence so the WHY is lost
acceptance_tests: the step writes weakness records with cause+evidence+fix, gamification day-completion percentages and self-metric snapshots as append-only dated data with no in-place mutation
revisit_triggers: a storage retention/rollup policy is needed
a consumer needs a new artifact field
an in-place mutation is discovered breaking idempotency

nodes.definition: Compose the go/no-go the whole KB builds toward: a nightly run is declared COMPLETE and valid only when ingest reconciled the day's events, the calibration snapshot was stored, the FSRS re-fit gate was respected (run or correctly skipped), well-measured weaknesses were diagnosed and their records emitted with a WHY, tomorrow's schedule was assembled within the time budget with capped probes, and the self-metrics were updated — all written append-only. Reconciled rules: never mutate history in place; never ship a plan when the pipeline is unhealthy (degrade to FSRS-only); never refit on thin data; never let probes crowd out learning; never log a bad card as a learner weakness; never conflate the acquisition target with the review-retention dial. A run that computed numbers but failed a gate is a no-go until the gate is cleared.

included: the completeness checklist across ingest, calibration, gated re-fit, diagnosis, schedule and self-metrics
the reconciled never-rules
the gate condition on declaring a run valid
excluded: the internal detail of each step (their own nodes)
downstream UI consumption of the artifacts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a gate change, a degraded-mode episode, or a new pipeline gate updates the run verdict

pros.claim: A single completeness verdict prevents declaring a run done when a gate silently failed
pros.example: withholding the done flag because the schedule blew the time budget or history was mutated

cons.claim: A strict all-gates verdict can block an otherwise-useful partial run
cons.example: failing a whole run for a self-metrics write hiccup when the schedule was fine

failure_modes: declaring a run complete while a gate (budget, idempotency, refit) failed
treating the verdict as static when a degraded-mode or threshold change alters it
acceptance_tests: the verdict confirms ingest, stored calibration, respected re-fit gate, emitted weakness records, in-budget schedule and updated self-metrics, enforces the never-rules, and conditions 'complete' on clearing every gate
revisit_triggers: a gate definition or threshold changes
degraded mode is triggered and the verdict must reflect it
a new pipeline step adds a gate to the checklist

edges.why_related: the job contract's idempotency and ordering rules govern how the ingest step is written
calibration must run over the reconciled, de-duplicated event stream ingest produces
the re-fit gate reads the calibration trend to decide whether to re-fit or revert
the BKT/Elo replay consumes the same reconciled concept-tagged answer stream
the confusion matrix is built from the same replayed answers and their wrong-entity content
weakness flags read the updated Elo theta, BKT P(L) and Glicko-style uncertainty
discrimination-failure pairs feed the misconception (E2) branch of the diagnosis
item-Elo difficulty outliers vs siblings come from the updated per-item d
the ~85% acquisition target is the anchor the rolling challenge band adjusts around
the Elo theta and item d are what let p(theta,d) be placed in the target band
the confused pairs are exactly what the interleaving policy places adjacent-but-not-identical
predicted load and the mastered-easy signal come from the FSRS S-distribution the calibration step exposes
the day's probe items are part of the content set the schedule assembles
the (possibly re-fit) FSRS parameters set the due reviews the schedule is built from
the interleaving policy supplies the ordering the schedule builder applies to its content set
the budget trim decides which items are postponed so the assembled plan fits the time budget
the current challenge band sets the p~=0.85 difficulty at which acquisition items are selected
the daily calibration snapshots are the trend the prediction loop tracks
the plan-of-record is what adherence is later measured against
the efficacy loop audits whether the weakness step's fixes produced recovery
the nightly single-card flags are aggregated into the loop's leech/outlier/template rates
job-completion and backlog signals come from the contracted pipeline's logs
the prediction-calibration scorecard is one of the governed self-metrics
diagnosis efficacy is the meta self-metric the scorecard governs
the assembled plan and its day-completion basis are written into the reporting artifacts
the completeness verdict confirms the artifacts were written append-only before declaring done
probe items for diagnosis compete with due reviews and new material for the day's limited budget
edges.resolution_rule: cap probe items to a few per day so diagnosis informs but never crowds out learning; when budget is tight, drop probes before dropping due reviews or weak-concept drills

edges.why_related: a fresh calibration gap tempts an immediate re-fit while thin data makes refitting add noise
edges.resolution_rule: keep the re-fit gated behind ~1000+ reviews and ~2-4 weeks since last fit and trust the trend not one snapshot; a single-day gap never triggers a re-fit

edges.why_related: pushing hard acquisition items at ~0.85 adds load while the budget trim wants to shed items to fit the time cap
edges.resolution_rule: protect weak-concept and acquisition items and satisfy the budget by postponing mastered-easy reviews first, never by dropping the challenge items

edges.why_related: the ~85% acquisition target and the FSRS ~0.9 review-retention dial are different quantities that are easy to conflate
edges.resolution_rule: keep the two dials strictly separate: ~80-85% governs new-material acquisition difficulty, FSRS desired_retention governs review scheduling; never tune one to hit the other's number

edges.why_related: a bad card and a real learner weakness both present as repeated lapses on a concept
edges.resolution_rule: route extreme predicted-vs-actual gaps, item-Elo outliers and leeches to the rewrite queue as card faults first, and only record a learner weakness once the card is cleared as sound

edges.why_related: when a fix class chronically fails to produce recovery, the efficacy loop adjusts the diagnosis thresholds and probe logic
a persistent calibration degradation triggers a re-fit and a post-fit worsening triggers a revert
chronically ~60%-done plans feed back to shrink the size of future assembled plans
a template-level fix changes the card pool the next nightly card-quality pass scores
an unhealthy pipeline constrains the schedule to degraded FSRS-only mode
interleaving the confused pairs causally drives the discrimination recovery the efficacy loop then measures
the in-budget assembled schedule is one of the gates the completeness verdict checks

conflict_axes.name: diagnosis_probes_vs_learning_budget
conflict_axes.description: Emitting probe items to resolve ambiguous weaknesses competes with due reviews and new material for the day's limited time budget.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cap probes to a few per day and drop them before due reviews or weak-concept drills when the budget is tight

conflict_axes.name: refit_freshness_vs_thin_data_noise
conflict_axes.description: Refitting FSRS parameters chases a better fit to recent behaviour but on thin single-user data adds noise that destabilizes scheduling.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate the re-fit behind ~1000+ reviews and ~2-4 weeks and revert if post-fit calibration worsens

conflict_axes.name: challenge_push_vs_time_budget
conflict_axes.description: Selecting hard acquisition items at the ~85% band adds load while the time budget wants fewer items.
poles: shed items to fit the budget
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: postpone mastered-easy reviews first and protect acquisition and weak-concept items

conflict_axes.name: acquisition_target_vs_review_retention_dial
conflict_axes.description: The ~85% new-material acquisition target and the FSRS ~0.9 review-retention dial measure different quantities and are easily conflated.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply ~80-85% only to acquisition difficulty and FSRS desired_retention only to review scheduling

conflict_axes.name: bad_card_vs_real_weakness
conflict_axes.description: Repeated lapses on a concept can mean a defective card or a genuine learner weakness, and mislabeling either corrupts both the card pool and the mastery estimate.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route outliers, leeches and extreme gaps to rewrite first and record a weakness only once the card is cleared as sound

conflict_axes.name: interleaving_benefit_vs_initial_encoding
conflict_axes.description: Interleaving trains discrimination but its benefit is smaller/mixed for some material and it can harm a topic's very first encoding.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: block only the initial encounter and interleave thereafter, prioritizing confused pairs

conflict_axes.name: in_session_fluency_vs_delayed_retrieval
conflict_axes.description: A session that feels smooth is a misleading signal; desirable-difficulty logic judges learning by delayed retrieval, not in-session ease.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never let the learner or scheduler optimize in-session fluency; calibrate difficulty to the delayed-retrieval target band

conflict_axes.name: full_analysis_vs_degraded_mode
conflict_axes.description: Running the full skill-model and diagnosis stack gives a richer plan but a failing pipeline must still deliver a valid plan.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: enter degraded FSRS-only mode on pipeline failure so the learner always gets a valid review plan

conflict_axes.name: metric_richness_vs_actionable_governance
conflict_axes.description: Tracking many self-metrics gives more visibility but a metric with no threshold or consumer is noise.
poles: keep only metrics with a named consumer
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require every metric to have a daily snapshot, a threshold and a named action or flag, and delete the rest

edge_cases.description: A late-arriving AI-graded voice answer is counted as a fresh attempt instead of updating its original review
edge_cases.trigger: a voice transcription is graded the morning after its review and re-enters ingest
edge_cases.mitigation: join late grades back to the original attempt by id and keep ingest idempotent so recall is not double-counted

edge_cases.description: A single noisy one-day calibration snapshot is read as real model degradation and triggers a premature re-fit
edge_cases.trigger: a thin decile swings the daily Brier score by chance
edge_cases.mitigation: act only on the multi-day trend and keep the re-fit gated behind the review-volume and recency thresholds

edge_cases.description: The FSRS optimizer is re-fit on ~300 reviews and overfits two weeks of thin data
edge_cases.trigger: a re-fit runs before the ~1000-review and ~2-4-week gate is met
edge_cases.mitigation: skip the re-fit until both thresholds are met and revert if post-fit calibration worsens

edge_cases.description: The Glicko rating-deviation update equations are hard-coded from memory despite being UNKNOWN in the research
edge_cases.trigger: an engineer fills the RD update with a half-remembered formula
edge_cases.mitigation: keep RD as a conceptual uncertainty proxy only and do not hard-code Glicko equations until glicko.net's canonical spec is fetched

edge_cases.description: An MCQ correct is treated as full mastery evidence, ignoring the ~25% four-option guessing floor
edge_cases.trigger: a 4-option MCQ correct updates BKT/Elo at the same weight as a free-recall correct
edge_cases.mitigation: down-weight MCQ corrects for the guessing floor so mastery evidence from typed/spoken recall counts more

edge_cases.description: An under-sampled concept is flagged as a real weakness on one or two answers
edge_cases.trigger: a concept with high uncertainty dips below the P(L) threshold on a single miss
edge_cases.mitigation: require low Glicko-style uncertainty as well as low theta/P(L) before flagging, and probe before remediating

edge_cases.description: Probe items accumulate until diagnosis crowds out due reviews and new material
edge_cases.trigger: many concepts stay ambiguous and each emits probes on the same night
edge_cases.mitigation: cap the daily probe budget and defer excess probes to later nights

edge_cases.description: A defective card everyone lapses on is recorded permanently as a learner weakness
edge_cases.trigger: an ambiguous or wrong card's lapses lower its concept's mastery estimate
edge_cases.mitigation: route leeches, item-Elo outliers and extreme predicted-vs-actual gaps to rewrite before recording any weakness

edge_cases.description: A chronically ~60%-done plan is read as a lazy learner rather than an oversized plan
edge_cases.trigger: planned items exceed what the learner completes for several days running
edge_cases.mitigation: treat a never-finished plan as a bad plan and shrink future plans to a finishable size

edge_cases.description: The nightly job crashes after the skill update but before scheduling and a re-run double-applies updates
edge_cases.trigger: a mid-job failure on a non-idempotent step
edge_cases.mitigation: make every step idempotent with append-only writes so a full re-run reproduces the same state

edge_cases.description: The analysis stack is down and an empty or corrupt plan is shipped to the learner
edge_cases.trigger: a skill-update or diagnosis step fails during the nightly run
edge_cases.mitigation: enter degraded mode and schedule on FSRS due reviews alone so a valid plan is always delivered

edge_cases.description: Mastered-easy cards are postponed every night in a busy week until their retention actually lapses
edge_cases.trigger: the budget trim runs many days in a row on the same easy cards
edge_cases.mitigation: bound how many consecutive nights a card may be postponed and force it back in before predicted-R drops too far

workflow.action: Establish the nightly job contract and ordering
workflow.description: Fix the inputs, the ordered idempotent steps, the nightly-vs-weekly cadence and the append-only write rule
workflow.gate: the four inputs, the step order, the cadence split and the crash-safe re-run guarantee are stated

workflow.action: Ingest and reconcile the day's events
workflow.description: Pull reviews and late graded voice answers, tag concepts, reconcile duplicates and joins
workflow.gate: the stream is concept-tagged, de-duplicated and identical on re-run with late grades joined to their attempts

workflow.description: Bin predicted R vs observed recall, score Brier/log-loss and store the daily snapshot
workflow.gate: the per-bin table, Brier/log-loss and a dated snapshot for the trend are produced

workflow.description: Run the optimizer only past the review-volume and recency thresholds, else skip, reverting on degradation
workflow.gate: the re-fit ran only at ~1000+ reviews and ~2-4 weeks or was skipped, with revert-on-degradation

workflow.description: Update BKT and Elo, down-weight MCQ corrects, decay Glicko-style uncertainty with the UNKNOWN-equations caveat
workflow.gate: BKT/Elo updated, MCQ guessing floor applied, Glicko equations marked UNKNOWN/not-hard-coded

workflow.action: Guard the skill fits and build the confusion matrix
workflow.description: Cap P(G)/P(S), catch Elo divergence, revert bad fits, and recompute the concept confusion matrix
workflow.gate: degenerate fits are frozen/reverted and off-diagonal confused pairs are flagged

workflow.description: Flag well-measured weak concepts, run the E1-E4 differential diagnosis, emit capped probes and weakness records
workflow.gate: only low-uncertainty weak concepts are flagged, causes assigned as far as data allows, probes capped

workflow.description: Detect leeches, item-Elo outliers and extreme predicted-vs-actual gaps and route them to rewrite
workflow.gate: bad cards go to the rewrite queue without lowering learner mastery

workflow.action: Set the acquisition target and re-calibrate the challenge band
workflow.description: Anchor on the ~85% target and adjust the band from the rolling 2-week actuals
workflow.gate: the band is set from rolling actuals with coasting-loosen/frustrated-tighten and kept separate from the FSRS retention dial

workflow.description: Combine due reviews + capped probes + new-material quota, order by interleaving, select at ~0.85, trim by postponing mastered-easy
workflow.gate: the plan fits the time budget, interleaves, hits the band, and degrades to FSRS-only if the pipeline is unhealthy

workflow.description: Refresh the calibration, adherence, diagnosis-efficacy, card-quality and pipeline-health scorecards under the snapshot+threshold+consumer rule
workflow.gate: every metric has a daily snapshot, a threshold and a named action or flag

workflow.action: Write reporting artifacts and declare the run go/no-go
workflow.description: Persist weakness records, day-completion percentages and self-metrics append-only, then check every gate
workflow.gate: artifacts are append-only and the run is declared complete only when every gate is cleared

priority_rationale: The job contract and idempotent ingest come first because every later step's correctness and re-runnability depend on an ordered, crash-safe pipeline over one reconciled event stream; retention calibration, the gated re-fit and the skill-model replay come next as the metrics and models the night recomputes; the confusion matrix, weakness diagnosis and card-quality pass then turn those models into flagged causes and card faults; the acquisition target, challenge calibration, interleaving order and load trim feed the schedule builder that assembles tomorrow's plan; the seven self-loops and their governing scorecard audit the predictor, scheduler and content factory; and the reporting-artifact write and the run go/no-go come last because they persist every upstream output append-only and declare the run complete only when every gate is cleared.

dominance_rules.rule: Idempotency dominates convenience in every step
dominance_rules.rationale: a crash mid-job must be safe to re-run, which only holds if no step mutates history in place
dominance_rules.trigger: a step is tempted to update a running tally or record in place
dominance_rules.action: write append-only dated snapshots and join late data by id so a full re-run reproduces the same state

dominance_rules.rule: The multi-day calibration trend dominates any single snapshot
dominance_rules.rationale: single-user daily bins are thin and noisy, so one snapshot cannot justify a re-fit
dominance_rules.action: act only on the persistent trend and keep the re-fit gated

dominance_rules.rule: The re-fit gate dominates a fresh calibration gap
dominance_rules.rationale: refitting on thin data adds noise that destabilizes scheduling more than a stale-but-stable model
dominance_rules.trigger: a calibration gap tempts an immediate re-fit
dominance_rules.action: hold the re-fit until ~1000+ reviews and ~2-4 weeks and revert if the post-fit calibration worsens

dominance_rules.rule: The UNKNOWN Glicko-equations blocker dominates memory
dominance_rules.rationale: the canonical Glicko update spec was egress-blocked in the research and must not be reconstructed from memory
dominance_rules.trigger: the rating-deviation update needs a formula
dominance_rules.action: use RD as a conceptual proxy only and fetch glicko.net before hard-coding any equation

dominance_rules.rationale: a card the learner's attempts all fail is more likely defective than proof of a real weakness
dominance_rules.trigger: repeated lapses cluster on a card
dominance_rules.action: route it to rewrite as a card fault first and record a weakness only once the card is cleared as sound

dominance_rules.rule: The learning budget dominates the probe budget
dominance_rules.rationale: diagnosis exists to serve learning, not to displace it
dominance_rules.trigger: probe items would crowd out due reviews or weak-concept drills
dominance_rules.action: cap probes to a few per day and drop excess probes before dropping learning items

dominance_rules.rule: Mastered-easy postponement dominates weak-concept postponement in the trim
dominance_rules.rationale: postponing high-stability easy cards costs the least predicted-R, while weak-concept cards are the point of the session
dominance_rules.trigger: the plan exceeds the time budget
dominance_rules.action: postpone mastered-easy reviews first and never trim weak-concept or acquisition items to fit

dominance_rules.rule: The degraded-mode fallback dominates a rich-but-broken plan
dominance_rules.rationale: a valid FSRS-only plan always beats an empty or corrupt one
dominance_rules.trigger: the pipeline is unhealthy during the nightly run
dominance_rules.action: schedule on FSRS due reviews alone and skip the skill-model and diagnosis steps until health returns

dominance_rules.rule: A named consumer dominates a metric's existence
dominance_rules.rationale: a metric with no threshold or action is noise that hides the signal
dominance_rules.trigger: a self-metric is tracked with no consumer
dominance_rules.action: give it a daily snapshot, a threshold and a named action or flag, or delete it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Make every step idempotent with append-only writes from the first implementation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mid-job crash double-applying updates and a costly reconstruction of corrupted history

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile late graded voice answers onto their original attempt at ingest
anti_rework_rules.prevents: double-counted recall that silently poisons calibration and every downstream skill flag

anti_rework_rules.rule: Gate the FSRS re-fit behind the review-volume and recency thresholds before running it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a noisy thin-data re-fit that destabilizes intervals and has to be reverted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat Glicko RD as an UNKNOWN-blocked proxy until the canonical spec is fetched
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hard-coding a wrong rating-deviation update that mis-ranks weakness certainty and must be ripped out

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the card-quality pass before recording weaknesses so bad cards are caught first
anti_rework_rules.prevents: permanently logging a defective card's failures as a learner weakness that later has to be unwound

anti_rework_rules.rule: Cap the daily probe budget when the schedule is assembled
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a probe flood crowding out learning and a day of low actual study that skews adherence

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the acquisition target and the FSRS review-retention dial separate from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mis-tuning both dials by conflating two different quantities and re-deriving them later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Wire degraded FSRS-only mode before shipping the analysis stack
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an outage delivering an empty or corrupt plan with no safe fallback in place

anti_rework_rules.rule: Give each self-metric a snapshot, threshold and consumer when it is first added
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an accumulation of orphan vanity metrics that must later be audited and deleted

iteration_protocol.trigger: the canonical Glicko update equations are fetched from glicko.net
iteration_protocol.action: replace the RD proxy with the real rating-deviation update and re-baseline the weakness-uncertainty flags

iteration_protocol.trigger: the multi-day calibration trend crosses its degradation threshold
iteration_protocol.action: trigger the gated FSRS re-fit and, if the post-fit calibration worsens, revert the parameters

iteration_protocol.trigger: a diagnosed fix class chronically fails to produce theta/P(L) recovery within K days
iteration_protocol.action: adjust the E1-E4 diagnosis thresholds and probe logic that produced that fix

iteration_protocol.trigger: a plan is completed only ~60% for several days running
iteration_protocol.action: shrink future plans to a finishable size and re-check next-week adherence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a whole card TEMPLATE type shows a high per-template error rate
iteration_protocol.action: fix the template once at the template level and re-measure the next card-quality pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: the rolling 2-week success rate leaves the target band (coasting >92% or frustrated <70%)
iteration_protocol.action: loosen or tighten the challenge band and re-select tomorrow's acquisition difficulty

iteration_protocol.trigger: the pipeline enters degraded mode or the voice-grading backlog ages past its alert threshold
iteration_protocol.action: alert, run FSRS-only scheduling, and review the run verdict for the degraded episode

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new answer format or grading source is added to the job
iteration_protocol.action: extend ingest reconciliation and the MCQ-style guessing-floor weighting for the new format

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
